intro: Welcome to the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum, in Şanlıurfa province, opened in 2015. This is the home of the finds from Göbekli Tepe and Karahan Tepe, and of the Balıklıgöl statue — the oldest known life-size sculpture of a human being.
history: Opened in 2015, the museum has the largest indoor exhibition area in Türkiye. Inside it, one of the enclosures of Göbekli Tepe has been rebuilt at excavation scale. The Neolithic hall keeps growing with finds from the region's 'Taş Tepeler' digs, and the Balıklıgöl statue stands on the same floor as the T-shaped pillars of Nevali Çori.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Balıklıgöl statue, the Göbekli Tepe reconstruction, the pillars of Nevali Çori, the Karahan Tepe finds and the mosaic hall.
facts: Did you know? The Balıklıgöl statue is about 11,000 years old, the oldest known life-size sculpture of a person. Its eyes were set with obsidian, yet it was never given a mouth. The museum has the largest indoor exhibition space in Türkiye, and inside it one of the enclosures of Göbekli Tepe has been rebuilt at full excavation scale.
outro: This brings our tour of the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
